diagnosis.summary: The nightly run for 2026-10-01 (run 4f54bd74) failed at the ingest step. Upstream sent payments.csv without the required contract column `method`, and no other column carries those values. This looks like a deliberate upstream drop, not a rename. Nothing in the pipeline can safely fix it, so I'm escalating to upstream_app_team to restore the column or confirm the new definition. analytics_engineering should be told that payment-method marts are affected.

root_cause.explanation: Upstream's 2026-10-01 payments.csv has 4 columns (payment_id, order_id, amount, paid_ts) instead of the 5 in the contract. `method` is gone, there is no new column in its place, and each data row has only 4 fields. Ingest's contract check correctly rejects the file with 'missing columns [method], unexpected columns []'. The 2026-09-30 file still had `method`, so the change started on 2026-10-01.

evidence.claim: Ingest failed on partition 2026-10-01 with a schema mismatch on raw.payments: method is missing and there are no unexpected columns.
The 2026-09-30 payments file had method. The 2026-10-01 file has only payment_id, order_id, amount and paid_ts, and no other field carries method values.
Nothing in the ingest config (column mappings or parsers) explains the failure; it uses defaults.
The other tables for 2026-10-01 arrived normally.

The runbook says a missing column with no unexpected column is an upstream drop. A dropped required column with no source must be escalated to upstream_app_team, not backfilled with defaults or NULLs and not mapped.
Asking upstream to resend the file would just reproduce the same file.

alternatives_considered: Column renamed (apply_column_mapping): ruled out. The file has no unexpected or new column and only 4 fields per row.
One-off export problem (request_upstream_redelivery): ruled out. The runbook says drops are persistent, so a resend would produce the same file.
rerun_only: wouldn't help, because the contract check would fail the same way.
ignore_extra_columns: doesn't apply. There are no extra columns, and this action can't drop contract columns.
Bad dbt model deploy: ruled out. The failure is in ingest, before any dbt models run.
Row-count drop (417 rows vs 439): about 5% fewer, within normal daily variation, and it doesn't cause the ingest failure.
